result.title: LARK: Lean-Assisted Reasoning for LLM-Generated GPU Kernels
result.summary: Efficient GPU kernels are typically low-level and hardware-specific, and LLM agents can now generate them faster than experts can verify. Existing approaches rely on testing, which provides evidence but not a guarantee of correctness. We introduce LARK, an agentic framework that automatically and formally verifies GPU kernels against their PyTorch reference implementations. LARK proves equivalence in functional and memory behavior under exact arithmetic and establishes a new trust boundary: human effort is only needed to verify operator-level Lean semantics ahead of kernel generation time, instead of checking every single line of generated code. LARK formalizes the GPU machine model and the semantics of each operation in Lean 4 once per target language, and the Lean 4 semantics of any incoming kernel is derived from these pre-built definitions. LLM agents then automate the proof in two steps. First, an agent decomposes the whole kernel semantics into smaller segments and Lean 4 verifies this segmentation, which addresses the intractability of proving equivalence for large kernels directly. Second, agents write Lean proofs that each kernel segment matches its high-level PyTorch counterpart. Together, the two steps give whole-program equivalence. We demonstrate that LARK can be used 1) to ensure correctness in existing code-generation agents and 2) to automatically verify human-written kernel libraries. On the KernelCraft GPU tasks, combined with a simple ReAct agent, LARK enables GLM 5.3 to fully verify 10 of 12 Level-1 kernels and Opus 5.5 all 5 Level-2 kernels. Moreover, over 10 production kernels randomly sampled from popular open-source LLM serving frameworks, LARK verifies 9 and identifies a new data race bug in the tenth. We believe LARK represents a significant step toward verifiable code generation in the agentic era.

AI.brief_summary: LARK 是一个针对 LLM 生成 GPU kernel 的 agentic 形式化验证框架：用 Lean 4 一次性形式化 GPU 机器模型与算子语义，再由 agent 把整体 kernel 语义拆成小片段、分别证明其与 PyTorch 参考实现等价，从而组合出全程序等价性，并在 KernelCraft 任务和真实推理框架 kernel 上验证，还发现了一个数据竞争 bug。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「预置形式语义 + 把整体拆成可机器检查的片段再组合」的流程，可能为 latent 推理轨迹的分步、可组合正确性验证与停止判据提供概念线索；但对象是代码等价性而非视觉推理状态，迁移价值需核查。
